title: Zorn's lemma for families of subsets
statement: Let $X$ be a set and $\mathcal S$ a set of subsets of $X$. Assume that every chain $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S$ (a subset of $\mathcal S$ any two members of which are comparable for inclusion; the empty chain included) has an upper bound in $\mathcal S$: a member $U\in\mathcal S$ with $C\subseteq U$ for every $C\in\mathcal C$. Then $\mathcal S$ has a maximal element: a member $M\in\mathcal S$ such that every $N\in\mathcal S$ with $M\subseteq N$ satisfies $N=M$.
